title: Finite-pattern factorization in a completed positive monoid algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, and let $P\subseteq G$ be an additive submonoid generated by finitely many elements. Let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a group homomorphism such that $w(p)>0$ for every $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$. Let $B=A^P$ be the ring of all coefficient families, with componentwise addition and convolution $(ab)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}a_ub_v$; these sums are finite under the stated hypotheses. Write $z^p$ for the family with coefficient $1$ at $p$ and $0$ elsewhere, and $C(a)=az^0$ for the constant embedding $A	o B$. Let $\mathfrak b\subseteq B$ be the ideal generated by $C(\mathfrak m)$ and the $z^p$ for $p
e0$. For $p
e0$, define $
u(p)$ to be the largest length of a decomposition of $p$ into nonzero elements of $P$ (a finite maximum under these hypotheses), and put $
u(0)=0$. For every integer $n\ge1$, every family $(a_p)_{p\in P}$ satisfying $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}$ for all $p$ belongs to $\mathfrak b^n$. Here an ideal power $I^k$ is the ideal of finite sums of products of $k$ elements of $I$, with $I^0$ the whole ring.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, together with the explicit finite-pattern factorization supplied here; the source does not state this coefficient refinement verbatim.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length] to $P,G,w,A$, after choosing a finite nonzero generator list. It supplies the attained function $
u$, $
u(0)=0$, the finite set $S_n=\{p:
u(p)<n\}$, and the convolution ring with its constant homomorphism and monomial formulas. Thus all the operations and decomposition lengths in the statement are well-defined.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; assembly of the agent-supplied coefficient refinement, old steps 1--3: positive weights, maximal decomposition length, finite bounded-weight sets, convolution ring laws and shift, and finite low-length support.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose a finite generator list for $\mathfrak m$, possibly empty. For $p\in S_n$ use an attained decomposition of length $l_p=\nu(p)<n$, given by [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length]; at $0$ use the empty decomposition. Apply [lem-trf-finite-support-monomial-ideal-power] with $J=\mathfrak m$, $S=S_n$, and the maps $C,z$ of step 1. Its hypotheses hold because $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{n-l_p}$. It gives $a^{<}=\sum_{p\in S_n}C(a_p)z^p\in\mathfrak b^n$. By the coefficient formula from step 1 this family agrees with $a$ on $S_n$ and is zero elsewhere.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; assembly of the agent-supplied coefficient refinement, old steps 4--5: finite ideal-generator expansion and finite low-length coefficient factorization, generalized to any commutative target ring and any finite set of chosen decompositions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-high-length-prefix-division] with the same nonzero generator list and $n$. Its finite shifted-sum identity expresses the family $a^{\ge n}$, equal to $a$ on the complement of $S_n$ and zero on $S_n$, as $\sum_{I\in T}z^{s_I}c^I$. For each $I$, its monomial identity writes $z^{s_I}$ as a product of exactly $n$ nonzero generator monomials. Each factor is in $\mathfrak b$ by definition, so multiplication by $c^I\in B$ and finite addition give $a^{\ge n}\in\mathfrak b^n$. For $P=\{0\}$ the tail and the tuple sum are both zero, as covered by the cited lemma.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; assembly of the agent-supplied coefficient refinement, old steps 6--7: coverage by generator prefixes, first-eligible partition, residual coefficient families and their finite shifted-sum identity.

proof.text: Coefficientwise $a=a^{<}+a^{\ge n}$, since $S_n$ and its complement partition $P$. The two summands belong to $\mathfrak b^n$ by steps 2 and 3, so closure of this ideal under addition proves $a\in\mathfrak b^n$.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; assembly of the agent-supplied coefficient refinement, last sentence of old step 7: the low-length and high-length parts are complementary and closure of $\mathfrak b^n$ under addition.

lean.statement: theorem finitePattern_factorization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (P : Type v) [AddCommMonoid P] [AddMonoid.FG P] (G : Type w) [AddCommGroup G] (ι : P →+ G) (hι : Function.Injective ι) (wgt : G →+ ℤ) (hpos : ∀ p : P, p ≠ 0 → 0 < wgt (ι p)) (hfree : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (G ≃+ (Fin r → ℤ))) : ∃ ν : P → ℕ, ν 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ p : P, IsGreatest {k : ℕ | ∃ f : Fin k → P, (∀ i : Fin k, f i ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ i, f i) = p} (ν p)) ∧ (∀ p : P, Set.Finite {q : P × P | q.1 + q.2 = p}) ∧ ∃ ring : CommRing (P → A), (∀ p : P, (@Zero.zero (P → A) ring.toZero) p = 0) ∧ (∀ p : P, (@One.one (P → A) ring.toOne) p = if p = 0 then 1 else 0) ∧ (∀ (a c : P → A) (p : P), (@Add.add (P → A) ring.toAdd a c) p = a p + c p) ∧ (∀ (a c : P → A) (p : P), (@Mul.mul (P → A) ring.toMul a c) p = ∑ᶠ q : {q : P × P // q.1 + q.2 = p}, a q.1.1 * c q.1.2) ∧ ∀ (b : @Ideal (P → A) ring.toSemiring), b = @Ideal.span (P → A) ring.toSemiring ({x : P → A | ∃ t : A, t ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ x = fun p ↦ if p = 0 then t else 0} ∪ {x : P → A | ∃ q : P, q ≠ 0 ∧ x = fun p ↦ if p = q then 1 else 0}) → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ a : P → A, (∀ p : P, a p ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ^ (n - ν p)) → a ∈ (@Ideal.instIdemCommSemiring (P → A) ring.toCommSemiring).toMonoid.npow n b
